en: The Philippines is an archipelago made up of exactly 7,641 islands, according to the latest official NAMRIA survey.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the country, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
Luzon is the largest island in the Philippines, covering a land area of approximately 109,965 square kilometers.
Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an 8.2-kilometer underground river that flows directly through a cave into the sea.
The Philippine Trench is the deepest ocean trench in the country, plunging to 10,540 meters at the Galathea Depth.
The San Juanico Bridge is the longest bridge in the Philippines, stretching exactly 2.16 kilometers across the San Juanico Strait.
The Philippines is currently divided into 17 administrative regions, including the National Capital Region and the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region.
Mount Mayon stands 2,462 meters tall and is the most active Philippine volcano with over 50 recorded historical eruptions.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers 97,030 hectares of protected marine habitat in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
Mount Pulag is the second highest peak at 2,928 meters, famous for its grassland peaks and sea of clouds.
